subject: Cooking
title: The Boston Tea Party: Tax, Tea, and Revolution
description: Learn The Boston Tea Party: Tax, Tea, and Revolution in one minute.

hook.text: In 1773, American colonists dumped 342 chests of British tea into Boston Harbor. A beverage started a revolution.

buildup.text: Britain's Tea Act gave the East India Company a monopoly on American tea sales — and imposed taxes without consent.

discovery.text: 'No taxation without representation' became the rallying cry. Tea symbolized British control over colonial commerce.

twist.text: After the protest, drinking tea became unpatriotic. Americans switched to coffee — a preference that persists today.

climax.text: The destroyed tea was worth over $1.7 million in today's money — the most expensive tea party in history.

punchline.text: America chose coffee over tea. The reason was politics, not taste.

quiz.question: Why did Americans switch from tea to coffee after 1773?
options: Drinking tea was seen as unpatriotic after the Boston Tea Party

details.summary: On December 16, 1773, colonists disguised as Mohawk Indians dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor to protest taxation without representation. The act destroyed 92,000 pounds of tea worth over $1.7 million today.
details.whyItMatters: The Boston Tea Party transformed a commodity dispute into a revolution. It shows how food taxation can become the trigger for political upheaval when it symbolizes broader injustice.
takeaways: 342 chests of tea worth $1.7 million today were dumped into the harbor
The act protested taxation without representation under the Tea Act
Britain's punitive Intolerable Acts united the colonies toward revolution

faq.question: Why was tea specifically chosen as the symbol of protest?
faq.answer: The Tea Act of 1773 gave the East India Company a monopoly on colonial tea sales with a tax the colonies had no voice in setting. Tea was consumed daily by most colonists, making the tax personally felt. Destroying tea made the economic and political protest visible and dramatic.

faq.question: Why did Americans switch from tea to coffee after the Revolution?
faq.answer: Drinking tea became unpatriotic after the Boston Tea Party. Coffee emerged as the patriotic alternative. John Adams declared tea drinking treasonous. Coffee consumption rose steadily. By the Civil War, coffee was the American national drink — a preference that persists 250 years later.
